title: Build an Agent Platform
description: Build a custom workflow engine to orchestrate AI agents, manage state, and execute tools.
learning_objectives: Design a state management system for agent memory
Implement a tool execution dispatcher to bridge LLM calls and code
Build a complete end-to-end agentic workflow from scratch
prerequisites: Knowledge of asynchronous programming in Python or TypeScript
Experience with LLM API function calling/tool definitions

sections.heading: Architecture of an Agent Platform
sections.content_brief: Explain the conceptual difference between a linear chain and an agentic loop. Introduce the 'ReAct' (Reason + Act) pattern as the foundation for the platform architecture.

sections.heading: Designing the State Manager
sections.content_brief: Implement a state object that tracks conversation history, tool outputs, and internal variables. Explain how this state acts as the 'short-term memory' passed back into the LLM context window.
sections.code_context: A State class that manages a list of messages and a key-value store for agent variables.

sections.heading: The Tool Dispatcher
sections.content_brief: Create a registry system where tools are defined as functions. Implement a dispatcher that takes the LLM's tool call request, matches it to the correct function, and executes it safely.
sections.code_context: A ToolRegistry class with methods to register functions and execute them by name using dynamic dispatch.

sections.heading: Implementing the Orchestration Loop
sections.content_brief: Build the core 'while' loop that manages the agent's lifecycle: calling the LLM, parsing tool requests, executing tools via the dispatcher, and feeding results back to the LLM until a final response is generated.
sections.code_context: The main agent loop implementing the Think-Act-Observe cycle.

sections.heading: End-to-End Example: A Research Agent
sections.content_brief: A concrete step-by-step walkthrough showing the full sequence from user input through each intermediate step (with actual values/messages) to final output. This will demonstrate a research agent using a mock search tool and a calculator.
sections.code_context: A full implementation combining the State Manager, Tool Dispatcher, and Loop to solve a multi-step query.

admonitions.content: Always implement a maximum iteration limit (e.g., 10 loops) in your orchestration engine to prevent infinite loops and runaway API costs if the agent gets stuck.
For production platforms, consider using a database like Redis or PostgreSQL for state management instead of in-memory objects to allow for persistence across sessions.
